name: Whitehorse Mountain
blurb: The mountain that fills Darrington's skyline: 6,000 ft of relief from the valley floor, finished on a small glacier and an exposed rock summit.
permit: Free self-issued wilderness permit. Mine Road and Forest Road 2030 lead to the Neiderprum trailhead.

routes.name: Northwest Shoulder
routes.grade: Grade II · snow, small glacier, class 3
routes.summary: The Neiderprum trail climbs brutally to an old mining-cabin meadow; a climbers route then follows the northwest shoulder on snow to the Whitehorse Glacier and a short, exposed scramble.
skills: A very long day of steep gain

line.source: Placed by hand on terrain data and published route descriptions; not surveyed

waypoints.name: Cabin meadow
waypoints.note: Site of the old mining cabin. The trail fades out beyond here.

waypoints.name: Northwest shoulder
waypoints.note: Snow or heather bivy sites on the shoulder.

sections.note: Neiderprum trail: very steep, rooty and overgrown in places. About 2,400 ft in a mile and a half.
Climbers route on snow (early season) or brush and talus up the northwest shoulder.
Small glacier and steep snowfields below the summit tower.
Exposed class 3 rock to the summit.
